questions.prompt: It is sharp and shiny. You use it to cut paper. What is it?

보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 종이를 자르는 날카롭고 반짝이는 물건은 scissors(가위)예요.

questions.prompt: Jina lost her new umbrella. She is ___.
hints: 물건을 잃어버리면 어떤 기분이 들까요?
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 새 우산을 잃어버렸으니 슬프겠지요. sad(슬픈)가 알맞아요.

questions.prompt: Ben heard a loud noise in the dark house. He is ___.
hints: 어두운 곳에서 갑자기 큰 소리가 들렸어요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 어두운 집에서 큰 소리를 들으면 무서워요. scared(무서워하는)가 알맞아요.

questions.prompt: The movie is very long, and nothing happens. Eun is ___.

questions.explanation: 아무 일도 일어나지 않는 긴 영화는 지루해요. bored(지루한)가 알맞아요.

questions.prompt: Today is my birthday, and my friends gave me presents. I feel ___.

보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 생일에 선물을 받으면 기뻐요. happy(행복한)가 알맞아요.

questions.prompt: All of Hana's friends moved to another town. Now she feels ___.

questions.explanation: 친구들이 모두 이사 가서 혼자라고 느끼니 lonely(외로운)가 알맞아요.

questions.prompt:
A: I'm sad. My dog is sick.

questions.explanation: 친구가 슬픈 소식을 말했으니 위로하는 I'm sorry to hear that.이 알맞아요.

questions.prompt:
A: I'm so happy! I got a new bike!

questions.explanation: 기쁜 소식에는 That's great!(잘됐다!)로 함께 기뻐해 줘요.

questions.prompt:
A: I'm cold.

questions.explanation: 추운 사람에게는 겉옷을 입으라고 하는 말이 알맞아요.

questions.prompt:

questions.explanation: 더운 사람에게는 선풍기를 켜자는 말이 알맞아요.

questions.prompt:
A: I'm scared of the dark.
B: ___

options.text: Turn off the light and close the door.
It is a sunny day, so let's play.
Don't worry. I'm here with you.
Let's go outside alone in the dark.

hints: 두려워하는 친구에게는 어떤 말이 힘이 될까요?

questions.explanation: 어둠이 무서운 친구에게는 안심시키는 말이 알맞아요.

questions.prompt:
A: ___
B: I feel much better, thanks.
hints: B의 대답에 'feel'이 들어 있어요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 기분이 나아졌다는 대답은 How do you feel now?(지금 기분이 어때?)에 대한 답이에요.

questions.prompt:
A: ___

questions.explanation: 생김새와 느낌을 말하는 대답은 What is it like?(그건 어떤 모습이야?)에 대한 답이에요.

questions.prompt:
A: ___

questions.explanation: 이유(because ...)를 말하는 대답이므로 Why로 시작하는 질문이 알맞아요.

questions.prompt: It is raining outside. What should you take?
hints: 비를 피하는 물건이 필요해요.

questions.explanation: 비가 올 때는 우산(an umbrella)을 가져가요.

questions.prompt: It is cold and snowy. Which clothes are best?

questions.explanation: 춥고 눈이 오면 두꺼운 외투와 장갑이 알맞아요.

questions.prompt:
Mon: sunny, 28°C
Tue: rainy, 20°C
Wed: windy, 18°C
Thu: cloudy, 19°C

questions.explanation: 비가 오는(rainy) 날은 Tuesday(화요일)예요.

questions.prompt:
Fri: snowy
Sat: windy
Sun: sunny
Mon: rainy

보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 바람이 부는(windy) 날은 Saturday(토요일)라서 연을 날리기 좋아요.

questions.prompt: Which word is different?

questions.explanation: rainy, sunny, windy는 날씨를 나타내고 sleepy(졸린)는 몸 상태를 나타내요.

questions.prompt: 다음 중 만졌을 때의 느낌을 나타내는 말이 아닌 것은?

보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: soft, hard, wet은 만졌을 때의 느낌이고 noisy(시끄러운)는 소리에 관한 말이에요.

questions.prompt:
A: Look! It's snowing!
B: ___

options.text: I want to wear my sandals.

hints: 눈 오는 날 입는 옷을 떠올려 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 눈이 오면 따뜻한 모자를 쓰자는 말이 알맞아요.

questions.prompt: I need a ___ jacket because it is very cold outside.
hints: 추운 날씨에 필요한 옷의 느낌을 생각해 보세요.

questions.explanation: 밖이 매우 추우니 따뜻한(warm) 재킷이 필요해요.

questions.prompt: '작은 노란 새'를 영어로 바르게 말한 것은?

questions.prompt: Sam says, “I have a ant on my hand.” What should he say?

questions.explanation: ant는 모음 소리로 시작하므로 an ant가 알맞아요.

questions.prompt:
A. Now he feels warm.
B. Ben feels cold.

What is the best order?

questions.prompt:

questions.prompt: The movie was very long, but the cartoon was ___.

questions.explanation: but으로 대조하므로 long(긴)과 반대 뜻인 short(짧은)가 알맞아요.

questions.prompt: In the zoo, the elephant is huge, but the mouse is ___.

보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: huge(아주 큰)와 대조되는 말은 tiny(아주 작은)예요.

questions.prompt: The soup was hot ten minutes ago. Now it is ___.

questions.explanation: 시간이 지나 식었으니 hot과 반대인 cold가 알맞아요.

questions.prompt: The river is shallow here, but over there it is ___.
hints: 수영할 때 발이 닿는 곳과 닿지 않는 곳을 떠올려 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: shallow(얕은)와 대조되는 말은 deep(깊은)이에요.

questions.prompt: Grandpa's hands are rough, but the baby's hands are ___.

questions.explanation: rough(거친)와 대조되는 아기 손의 느낌은 soft(부드러운)예요.

questions.prompt: Min-ho's shoes are too small. He needs a ___ pair.
hints: 작은 신발 대신 어떤 크기가 필요할까요?
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 신발이 너무 작으니 더 큰(big) 신발이 필요해요.

questions.prompt:

B: ___

options.text: Its name is Nabi, and it is mine.
It is two years old this month.
It is sleeping on the sofa now.
It is small and very friendly.

hints: 'like' 질문은 이름이나 나이를 묻는 것이 아니에요.

questions.explanation: What is ... like?는 성격이나 모습을 묻는 질문이라 모습·성격으로 답해야 해요.

questions.prompt:
A: You look worried. What's wrong?
B: ___

options.text: It is sunny and warm today.
I have a big test tomorrow.
I am a student at this school.

hints: A가 걱정스러워 보이는 이유를 묻고 있어요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 무슨 일이냐는 질문에는 걱정하는 이유를 말해야 해요.

questions.prompt:
A: How does the blanket feel?
B: ___
hints: 'feel'은 만졌을 때의 느낌을 물어요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 담요의 촉감을 묻는 질문에는 soft(부드러운)가 알맞아요.

questions.prompt: 공원 바닥에 이런 표지판이 있어요: “WET FLOOR. Walk slowly.” 알맞은 뜻은?
hints: wet과 slowly의 뜻을 먼저 떠올려 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: WET FLOOR는 젖은 바닥이라는 경고이고 Walk slowly는 천천히 걸으라는 말이에요.

questions.prompt:
Menu: Cold milk / Hot chocolate / Orange juice / Lemon ice tea

Ana is cold. She wants a hot drink. What should she order?
hints: 메뉴 이름에 온도를 나타내는 말이 있어요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 뜨거운 음료는 Hot chocolate뿐이에요.

questions.prompt: In “My bag is light, so I can carry it easily,” the word “light” means ___.
hints: 뒤에 나오는 'carry it easily'에 주목하세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 가방을 쉽게 들 수 있다고 했으니 light는 '가벼운'이라는 뜻이에요.

questions.prompt: 다음 중 문법적으로 옳은 문장은?

options.text: She has a small red bag.
She has red a small bag.
She has a small red bags.
She has a small bag red.

hints: 네 문장에서 서로 다른 부분에 동그라미를 치고 그 부분만 비교해 보세요.
명사 앞에서 형용사가 어떤 순서로 오는지 생각해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 정답: “She has a small red bag.” (그녀는 작은 빨간 가방을 가지고 있어요.) 형용사는 명사 바로 앞에 와요. a 다음에 형용사(small, red)를 쓰고, 가방이 한 개이므로 명사는 bag으로 단수로 써요.

questions.prompt:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
She has a small ___ bag.
(그녀는 작은 빨간 가방을 가지고 있어요.)
hints: 빈칸 바로 앞의 “small”, 바로 뒤의 “bag”에 어울리는 말을 찾아보세요.
명사 앞에서 형용사가 어떤 순서로 오는지 생각해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 정답: “She has a small red bag.” (그녀는 작은 빨간 가방을 가지고 있어요.) 형용사는 명사 바로 앞에 와요. a 다음에 형용사(small, red)를 쓰고, 가방이 한 개이므로 명사는 bag으로 단수로 써요.

questions.prompt: 다음 중 문법적으로 옳은 문장은?

options.text: The kittens are very a small.

hints: 네 문장에서 서로 다른 부분에 동그라미를 치고 그 부분만 비교해 보세요.
주어가 하나인지 여럿인지 보세요.
questions.explanation: 정답: “The kittens are very small.” (새끼 고양이들은 아주 작아요.) 복수 주어(kittens)에는 are를 쓰고, 형용사에는 -s를 붙이지 않아요.

questions.prompt:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
The kittens ___ very small.
(새끼 고양이들은 아주 작아요.)
hints: 빈칸 바로 앞의 “kittens”, 바로 뒤의 “very”에 어울리는 말을 찾아보세요.
주어가 하나인지 여럿인지 보세요.
questions.explanation: 정답: “The kittens are very small.” (새끼 고양이들은 아주 작아요.) 복수 주어(kittens)에는 are를 쓰고, 형용사에는 -s를 붙이지 않아요.

questions.prompt: 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하세요. (새끼 고양이들은 아주 작아요.)

questions.prompt: Mina wants to leave the classroom to drink some water. What should she ask her teacher?

options.text: You should get some water, please?
Do I may get some water?

보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 허락을 구할 때는 May I ...?로 물어요. 'Yes, you may...'는 허락을 해 주는 대답이에요.

questions.prompt: A girl asks a dog's owner, "May I take a picture of your dog?" The owner agrees. What does the owner say?

options.text: Yes, you may not. Go ahead.

hints: 개 주인은 사진을 찍어도 되는지 묻는 말을 들었어요. 허락해 주는 말을 찾으세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 'Of course. Please do!'는 사진을 찍어도 좋다고 허락하는 자연스러운 대답이에요. 'Yes, you may not.'은 허락과 금지가 서로 모순되고, 'No, thank you.'는 거절하는 말이에요. 'You may, I take it.'은 문장이 어색해요.

questions.prompt: A: May I watch TV now? B: ___ Finish your homework first.

options.text: Sorry, may I ask you please?

hints: TV를 보려는 사람에게 '안 돼'라고 말해야 해요. 누가 허락하는 사람인지 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 허락을 구한 사람에게 거절할 때는 'you may not'을 써요. B가 허락하는 사람이므로 주어는 you예요.

questions.prompt: The coach says, "You may leave early today." What does this mean?
hints: may는 '해도 좋다'는 허락이에요. 의무나 충고와 구별해 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: may는 허락을 뜻해서 'You may leave early.'는 일찍 가도 좋다는 말이에요.

questions.prompt: Which sentence asks someone else to do something for you, not for permission?

options.text: May I leave my bag here?
Can I put my bag here?

보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: Can you ...?는 상대에게 부탁하는 말이고, May I/Can I ...?는 내가 허락을 구하는 말이에요.

questions.prompt: Tom has a bad toothache. Which advice is best?

options.text: You should play outside all night.
You shouldn't go to a dentist.

hints: 이가 아플 때 도움이 되는 조언은 무엇일까요?

questions.explanation: 이가 아플 때는 치과에 가는 것이 알맞은 조언이에요. 나머지는 상황에 도움이 되지 않아요.

questions.prompt: A: I can't sleep at night. B: ___

options.text: You should drink more cola tonight.
You can't sleep well without a lot of cola.
You must drink cola before bed.
You shouldn't drink cola before bed.

hints: 잠이 안 오는 친구에게 도움이 되는 조언을 고르세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 콜라를 자기 전에 마시지 않는 게 좋다는 조언이 알맞아요. 나머지는 문제를 더 나쁘게 하거나 조언이 아니에요.

questions.prompt: Sue's new shoes are too small. She ___ wear them on a long hike.
hints: 작은 신발로 오래 걷는다면 좋은 생각일까요, 아닐까요?
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 신발이 작으면 긴 산행에 신지 않는 게 좋아요. 그래서 충고의 부정 shouldn't가 알맞아요.

questions.prompt: It is snowing and very cold. Which advice is NOT good?

hints: 눈이 오는 추운 날에 어울리지 않는 조언 하나를 찾으세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 추운 날 반바지와 티셔츠를 입으라는 조언만 상황에 맞지 않아요.

questions.prompt: '너무 많이 먹지 않는 게 좋아요.'를 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?

questions.explanation: '~하지 않는 게 좋다'는 shouldn't 뒤에 동사원형을 써서 You shouldn't eat too much.가 돼요.

questions.prompt: Which sentence gives friendly advice, not a rule?

options.text: Visitors may not feed the animals.

hints: 규칙은 어기면 안 되는 말이고, 조언은 권하는 말이에요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: should는 부드러운 조언이고, must나 may not은 규칙에 쓰여요.

questions.prompt: A sign at a park says, "Keep Off the Grass." Which sentence matches it?

options.text: You should walk on the grass.

questions.explanation: Keep Off the Grass는 잔디 위를 걸으면 안 된다는 뜻이라 You can't walk on the grass.와 같아요.

questions.prompt: A sign on a boat says, "Life jackets required." Which sentence matches it?

questions.explanation: required(필수)는 반드시 해야 한다는 뜻이라 must wear를 써요.

questions.explanation: 사진은 허용되지만 플래시는 쓰면 안 된다는 뜻이에요.

questions.prompt: A notice says, "Visitors should take off their muddy boots." What does it mean?

questions.explanation: 주유소에서 휴대폰을 꺼야 하니 사용하면 안 된다는 must not이 알맞아요.

questions.prompt: A: Where is Dad? B: I'm not sure. He ___ be in the garden.

questions.prompt: What does "Our team might win the game" mean?

questions.prompt: Which sentence says something is possible, but not sure?

We will go to the beach tomorrow.

questions.explanation: might는 가능성을 뜻해서 갈지도 모른다는 말이 돼요.

questions.prompt: '비가 올지도 몰라서 우산을 가져가는 게 좋겠어요.'를 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?

questions.explanation: 가능성은 may, 조언은 should로 말해요.

questions.prompt: Which sentence sounds like a strict rule, not friendly advice?

options.text: You must show your ticket at the gate.
I think you should try this soup.

hints: 어기면 안 되는 규칙으로 들리는 문장은 어느 것일까요?

questions.explanation: must는 규칙이나 꼭 해야 할 일이고, should는 부드러운 조언이에요.

questions.prompt: Ben forgot his swim cap. The pool rule says everyone needs one. What does the lifeguard say?

options.text: You can't wear a swim cap.
You must wear a swim cap.
You may wear a swim cap.
You might wear a swim cap.

hints: 수영장 규칙이 있는 상황이에요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 모두에게 필요한 규칙이므로 must를 써요.

questions.prompt: must와 비교할 때, should의 뜻을 바르게 설명한 것은?

options.text: should는 '~할 수 있다'는 능력을 나타내는 말이다.

hints: should와 must 중 어느 쪽이 더 약하고 부드러운 말인지 생각해 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: should는 '~하는 게 좋다'는 부드러운 조언이고, must는 규칙이나 의무예요.

questions.prompt: A: Can I eat in class? B: No. You ___ eat in class. It's the rule.
hints: 규칙으로 금지하는 상황이에요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 규칙으로 금지할 때는 must not을 써요.

questions.prompt: Sora wrote, "She cans swim fast." How can she fix it?
hints: can은 주어가 She여도 모양이 변하지 않아요.

questions.explanation: 조동사 can은 -s를 붙이지 않고 뒤에는 동사원형 swim을 써요.

questions.prompt: Minho wrote, "He must to go home now." How can he fix it?
hints: must 바로 뒤에 어떤 모양의 동사가 오는지 생각해 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: must 뒤에는 to 없이 동사원형이 와서 He must go home now.가 돼요.

questions.prompt: Yuna wrote, "Do you can ride a horse?" How can she fix it?

Do you can to ride a horse?

questions.explanation: can이 있는 질문은 do를 쓰지 않고 Can you ...?로 말해요.

questions.prompt: Dad wrote, "I don't can find my keys." How can he fix it?

보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: can의 부정은 can't이고 뒤에는 동사원형이 와요.

questions.prompt: Jisu wrote, "Where I should put my coat?" How can she fix it?

options.text: Where I put should my coat?
Where should put I my coat?
Where should I put my coat?
Where do I should put my coat?

questions.explanation: 의문사 뒤에 should가 오고 그 다음에 주어 I가 와요.

questions.prompt: Hajun wrote, "She should not goes out in the rain." Which is correct?

options.text: She should not go out in the rain.
She not should go out in the rain.
She should not going out in the rain.
She should not to go out in the rain.

questions.prompt: At the airport, the officer looked at my photo and name page and stamped it. It was my ___.
hints: 사진과 이름이 적힌 여행 서류를 떠올려 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 사진과 이름이 있고 공항에서 도장을 찍는 것은 passport(여권)예요.

questions.prompt: You buy a ticket here, wait on the platform, and then get on a train. Where are you?
hints: 기차를 타기 전에 하는 일들이 모두 한 장소에서 이루어져요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 표를 사고 승강장에서 기차를 기다리는 곳은 train station(기차역)이에요.

questions.prompt: Heavy snow fell, so our bus left two hours later than planned. The bus was ___.
hints: 'later than planned'가 어떤 상태를 말하는지 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 예정보다 늦게 출발한 것은 delayed(지연된)라고 해요.

questions.prompt: Which word does NOT belong with the others? violin, flute, drum, racket
hints: 소리를 내는 것과 공을 치는 것으로 나눠 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: violin, flute, drum은 악기이고 racket은 운동 도구예요.

questions.prompt: The robot club needs new members. If you want to join, ___ up before Friday.
hints: 동아리에 들어가려면 이름을 적어 신청해야 해요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: sign up은 '신청하다, 등록하다'라는 뜻으로 동아리에 가입할 때 써요.

questions.prompt: In ___ class, we study plants, magnets, and the moon.
hints: 배우는 내용이 어떤 과목에 해당하는지 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 식물, 자석, 달을 배우는 과목은 science(과학)예요.

questions.prompt: NOTICE: Sports Day is on Friday. Please wear your ___ and bring a water bottle.
hints: 운동회 날 몸을 움직이기 편한 옷이 어떤 것인지 생각해 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 운동회에는 활동하기 편한 gym clothes(체육복)를 입어요.

questions.prompt: Which word does NOT belong with the others? quiz, exam, test, picnic
hints: 학교에서 점수를 매기는 것과 놀러 가는 것을 구분해 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: quiz, exam, test는 실력을 확인하는 시험이고 picnic은 소풍이에요.

questions.prompt: Always wear a ___ when you ride a bike, because it protects your head.
hints: 'protects your head'가 단서예요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 머리를 보호하려고 쓰는 안전 장비는 helmet(헬멧)이에요.

questions.prompt: Dear parents, Please keep your child at home if your child has a ___ or keeps coughing.
hints: 'keeps coughing'과 같이 아플 때 나타나는 증상이에요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 기침과 함께 아프다는 신호가 되는 것은 fever(열)예요.

questions.prompt: Instead of throwing away a glass jar, Tom ___ it as a pencil holder.
hints: 'Instead of throwing away'와 이어지는 행동을 찾아보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: reuse는 '다시 사용하다'라는 뜻이에요. 버리지 않고 연필꽂이로 다시 쓴 거예요.

questions.prompt: Smoke from cars and factories makes the air dirty. This problem is called air ___.
hints: 공기가 더러워지는 문제의 이름을 찾아보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 공기를 더럽히는 문제는 air pollution(대기 오염)이에요.

questions.prompt: SAVE WATER: Please turn off the tap while you brush your teeth. Do not ___ water.
hints: 'SAVE WATER'라는 제목과 어울리는 말이 필요해요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 물을 아끼자는 안내이므로 Do not waste water(물을 낭비하지 마세요)가 알맞아요.

questions.prompt: Which word does NOT belong with the others? plastic bottle, newspaper, glass jar, banana peel
hints: 재활용품 분리함에 넣을 수 없는 것을 찾아보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 나머지는 재활용할 수 있지만 banana peel은 음식물 쓰레기예요.

questions.prompt: The jacket was $40, but this week it is half price. It is on ___.
hints: 'half price'가 어떤 상황인지 생각해 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 값을 깎아 파는 것을 on sale(할인 중)이라고 해요.

questions.prompt: Keep your ___ in case you need to return the shoes to the store.
hints: 가게에 신발을 돌려줄 때 보여 주는 종이가 무엇일까요?
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 물건을 산 증거인 receipt(영수증)가 있어야 환불할 수 있어요.

questions.prompt: Menu: Sandwich $4, Juice $2, Set (sandwich + juice) $5. Dan wants both a sandwich and a juice. What is the cheapest way to get both?

options.text: Order the set and an extra juice for $7

hints: 샌드위치와 주스를 모두 얻는 방법의 값을 비교해 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 샌드위치와 주스를 따로 사면 $6이고 세트는 $5라서 세트가 가장 싸요. 나머지는 더 비싸요.

questions.prompt: At the festival, we hung colorful paper ___ on the trees and lit them at night.
hints: 'lit them at night'로 어떤 물건인지 알 수 있어요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 밤에 불을 밝히는 종이 장식은 lantern(등)이에요.

questions.prompt: Bands, dancers, and big colorful floats moved slowly down the main street in the ___.
hints: 거리에서 행진하는 행사의 이름을 떠올려 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 거리를 따라 행진하는 행사는 parade(퍼레이드)예요.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses 'light' to mean 'not heavy'?

options.text: The traffic light is red, so cars must stop.
This bag is light, so I can carry it easily.
Please turn off the light before you leave.
The light in the room is warm and soft.

hints: 물건을 쉽게 들 수 있는 문장을 찾아보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: light는 '가벼운'이라는 뜻으로도 써요. 쉽게 들 수 있다는 말과 어울려요.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses 'watch' as a noun?

options.text: We will watch the fireworks from the hill.
I watch funny cartoons on TV after school.
Dad gave me a new watch for my birthday.
Please watch your little brother at the park.

hints: 문제가 무엇을 묻는지 한 문장으로 말해 본 뒤 보기를 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 'a new watch'의 watch는 손목시계라는 명사예요. 나머지는 '보다, 지켜보다'라는 동사예요.

questions.prompt: In 'My aunt runs a small flower shop,' what does 'runs' mean?
hints: 가게와 함께 쓰인 run은 어떤 뜻일까요?
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: run a shop은 가게를 운영한다는 뜻이에요.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses 'fly' for an insect?

options.text: Pilots fly big planes across the ocean.
A fly was sitting on my sandwich.
I want to fly my new kite at the park.
Many birds fly south when winter comes.

hints: a 뒤에서 샌드위치 위에 앉아 있는 대상이 무엇인지 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: A fly는 곤충 파리예요. 나머지 문장의 fly는 '날다, 날리다'라는 동사예요.

questions.prompt: The bear scratched the bark of the old pine tree. In this sentence, what does 'bark' mean?
hints: 곰이 발톱으로 긁은 대상을 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 소나무(pine tree)에 대한 이야기이므로 bark는 나무껍질이에요.

questions.prompt: Rui has the main part in the school play next week. Here, 'play' means ___.
hints: 'the main part'(주연)가 단서예요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: main part가 있는 school play는 연극이에요.

questions.prompt: Which word is made from 'rain' and 'coat' and is worn on a wet day?
hints: 두 낱말의 뜻을 합쳐 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: rain과 coat을 합친 raincoat은 비 오는 날 입는 옷이에요.

questions.prompt: Which word is NOT a compound word?
hints: 두 개의 독립된 낱말로 나뉘는지 살펴보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: teacher는 teach에 -er을 붙인 말이에요. 나머지는 두 낱말이 합쳐진 낱말이에요.

questions.prompt: The sun was so bright at the beach that I put on my ___ to protect my eyes.
hints: 'protect my eyes'에 어울리는 물건을 찾아보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 눈을 보호하려고 쓰는 것은 sun+glasses, 즉 선글라스예요.

questions.prompt: The door was locked, so Dad used a key to ___ it.
hints: 잠긴 문을 열 때의 동작을 나타내는 낱말을 만들어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: un-은 반대의 동작을 나타내요. unlock은 잠긴 것을 연다는 뜻이고 to 뒤에는 동사 원형이 와요.

questions.prompt: A person who teaches is a teacher. A person who dances as a job is a ___.
hints: teacher처럼 '~하는 사람'을 나타내는 끝부분을 떠올려 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: -er을 붙이면 '~하는 사람'이 돼요. dance+r = dancer예요.

questions.prompt: The garden was full of red, yellow, and purple flowers. It was a very ___ garden.
hints: 색이 많으면 어떤 접미사가 알맞을까요?
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: -ful은 '~이 가득한'이라는 뜻이라서 colorful은 색이 풍부하다는 말이에요. colorless는 색이 없다는 뜻이에요.

questions.prompt: My map was messy, so I will ___ it on a clean sheet of paper.
hints: '다시 그리다'를 만드는 앞부분을 붙여 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: re-는 '다시'라는 뜻이라서 redraw는 다시 그린다는 뜻이에요.

questions.prompt: Thank you for your ___ when I was lost.
hints: your 뒤에 어떤 품사가 와야 하는지 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: -ness를 붙이면 명사가 돼요. your 뒤에는 명사 kindness가 와요.

questions.prompt: After dinner, we like to ___ a walk by the river.
hints: '산책하다'에 어울리는 동사를 골라 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 산책하다는 take a walk라고 말해요.

questions.prompt: At the festival, kids ___ a wish and tie it to a tree.
hints: '소원을 빌다'와 함께 쓰는 동사를 떠올려 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 소원을 빌다는 make a wish라고 해요.

questions.prompt: We ___ a wonderful time on our trip to the sea.
hints: '즐거운 시간을 보내다'와 함께 쓰는 동사를 떠올려 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 즐거운 시간을 보내다는 have a wonderful time이고, 과거라서 had예요.

questions.prompt: Don't worry about winning. Just ___ your best.
hints: '최선을 다하다'라는 표현을 떠올려 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 최선을 다하다는 do one's best예요.

questions.prompt: It is easy to ___ friends in a new class if you smile.
hints: '친구를 사귀다'에 쓰는 동사를 골라 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 친구를 사귀다는 make friends라고 해요.

questions.prompt: NOTICE: The pool is ___ today for cleaning. Please come back tomorrow.
hints: 'Please come back tomorrow'가 단서예요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 청소 때문에 내일 다시 오라는 안내이므로 closed(문을 닫은)가 알맞아요.

questions.prompt: Hi Sora, I can't come to your party because I have a dentist appointment. I'm really ___.
hints: 파티에 못 가는 사람이 하고 싶은 말을 생각해 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 못 가서 미안한 마음을 표현하는 말은 sorry예요.

questions.prompt: SIGN in the library: Please be ___. Others are reading.
hints: 'Others are reading'이 이유예요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 다른 사람이 책을 읽고 있으니 quiet(조용한)해야 해요.

questions.prompt: FOUND: a red scarf near the gym. Please ___ the office to get it back.
hints: 스카프를 되찾기 위해 사무실에서 해야 할 일을 생각해 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 잃어버린 물건을 찾으려면 사무실에 들러야 해요. visit the office가 자연스러워요.

questions.prompt: 다음 중 문법적으로 옳은 문장은?

options.text: My sister makes yoga on Saturdays.
My sister doing yoga on Saturdays.
My sister does yoga on Saturdays.
My sister do yoga on Saturdays.

hints: 네 문장은 세 번째 낱말 부근이 서로 달라요. 그 부분을 비교해 보세요.
운동이나 활동 이름 앞에는 어떤 동사를 쓰는지 떠올려 보세요.
questions.explanation: 정답: “My sister does yoga on Saturdays.” (내 여동생은 토요일마다 요가를 해요.) '요가를 하다'는 do yoga라고 해요. 주어가 3인칭 단수이면 does를 써요.

questions.prompt:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
My sister ___ yoga on Saturdays.
(내 여동생은 토요일마다 요가를 해요.)
hints: 빈칸 바로 앞의 “sister”, 바로 뒤의 “yoga”에 어울리는 말을 찾아보세요.
운동이나 활동 이름 앞에는 어떤 동사를 쓰는지 떠올려 보세요.
questions.explanation: 정답: “My sister does yoga on Saturdays.” (내 여동생은 토요일마다 요가를 해요.) '요가를 하다'는 do yoga라고 해요. 주어가 3인칭 단수이면 does를 써요.

questions.prompt: 다음 중 문법적으로 옳은 문장은?

options.text: Please careful with the hot soup.
Please be carefully with the hot soup.
Please be care with the hot soup.
Please be careful with the hot soup.

She do not like cold milk.
She does not likes cold milk.
She does not like cold milk.

hints: 네 문장에서 서로 다른 부분에 동그라미를 치고 그 부분만 비교해 보세요.
does not 뒤의 동사 모양을 생각해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 정답: “She does not like cold milk.” (그녀는 차가운 우유를 좋아하지 않아요.) does not 뒤에는 동사의 원래 모양을 써요.

questions.prompt:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
She does not ___ cold milk.
(그녀는 차가운 우유를 좋아하지 않아요.)
hints: 빈칸 바로 앞의 “not”, 바로 뒤의 “cold”에 어울리는 말을 찾아보세요.
does not 뒤의 동사 모양을 생각해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 정답: “She does not like cold milk.” (그녀는 차가운 우유를 좋아하지 않아요.) does not 뒤에는 동사의 원래 모양을 써요.

questions.prompt: 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하세요. (그녀는 차가운 우유를 좋아하지 않아요.)
hints: 낱말이 모두 6개예요. 마침표로 끝나는 문장이에요.
첫 단어: “She”
questions.explanation: 정답: “She does not like cold milk.” (그녀는 차가운 우유를 좋아하지 않아요.) does not 뒤에는 동사의 원래 모양을 써요.

questions.prompt: 다음 중 sh 소리(/sh/, '쉬')로 시작하는 낱말은?
hints: s 한 글자가 아니라 s와 h 두 글자가 함께 내는 소리를 찾아요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: shell의 sh는 s와 h가 만나 '쉬' 소리 하나를 내요.

questions.prompt: 다음 중 ch 소리(/ch/, '치')로 시작하는 낱말은?
hints: c와 h가 나란히 있는 낱말이 어느 것인지 살펴보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: chick의 ch는 '치' 소리예요. sick은 /s/, kick은 /k/, quick은 /kw/로 시작해요.

questions.prompt: 다음 중 th가 낱말의 처음이나 끝이 아니라 가운데에 있는 것은?
hints: th의 위치가 어디인지 낱말마다 확인해 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: mother는 mo-ther처럼 th가 가운데에 있어요. tooth와 bath는 끝에, three는 처음에 있어요.

questions.prompt: 다음 중 wh로 시작하는 낱말은?
hints: w 바로 뒤에 h가 붙어 있는 낱말을 찾아요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: white는 w 바로 뒤에 h가 와요. wind, write, worm은 w 다음에 다른 글자가 와요.

questions.prompt: 다음 중 bl로 시작하는 낱말은?
hints: b 다음에 r이 아니라 l이 오는 낱말이에요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: blue는 b 다음에 l이 와서 bl 소리로 시작해요. 나머지는 br로 시작해요.

questions.prompt: 다음 중 st로 시작하는 낱말은?
hints: 모두 s로 시작하지만 s 바로 다음 글자가 달라요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: stamp는 s와 t가 이어져 st 소리로 시작해요. swim은 sw, snow는 sn, slide는 sl로 시작해요.

questions.prompt: 다음 중 tr로 시작하지 않는 낱말은?
hints: '아닌 것'을 찾는 문제예요. 첫 두 글자를 하나씩 확인해요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: drum은 dr로 시작해요. trip, tray, trap은 모두 tr로 시작해요.

questions.prompt: I start with the letters cl. I am white and float in the sky. What am I?
hints: cl로 시작하는 낱말이 모두 정답 후보예요. 하늘에 뜨는 것이 힌트예요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 하늘에 떠 있는 하얀 것은 cloud(구름)예요. 나머지도 cl로 시작하지만 하늘에 뜨지 않아요.

questions.prompt: bench는 글자가 5개예요. ch가 하나의 소리를 낸다면 bench의 소리는 모두 몇 개일까요?
hints: 글자 수가 아니라 소리 수를 세요. ch는 한 덩어리예요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: bench는 /b/ /e/ /n/ /ch/ 네 소리예요. ch 두 글자가 소리 하나를 내요.

questions.prompt: mad 끝에 e를 붙이고 a를 알파벳 이름처럼 읽으면 어떤 낱말이 될까요?
hints: 끝에 붙은 e는 소리 나지 않지만 모음 소리를 바꿔 줘요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: mad에 e를 붙인 made는 a를 /에이/처럼 읽는 낱말이에요.

questions.prompt: o가 알파벳 이름처럼 /오우/로 소리 나는 낱말은?
hints: 끝에 e가 있는 낱말이 하나 있어요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: nose는 o-e 짜임이라 o를 /오우/로 읽어요. pot, box, dog의 o는 짧게 읽어요.

questions.prompt: u가 알파벳 이름처럼 /유/로 소리 나는 낱말은?
hints: u 다음에 자음 하나, 그 뒤에 e가 오는 짜임을 찾아요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: cube는 u-e 짜임이라 u를 /유/로 읽어요. jump, bus, sun의 u는 짧은 /어/ 소리예요.

questions.prompt: tap과 tape를 비교한 설명으로 알맞은 것은?

options.text: tape의 a는 알파벳 이름처럼 읽고, 끝의 e는 소리 내지 않아요.
tape는 끝의 e를 /에/ 소리로 읽고, a는 짧게 읽어요.
tap과 tape는 글자만 다르고 모음 소리는 완전히 같아요.
tap의 a는 알파벳 이름처럼 읽고, tape의 a는 짧게 읽어요.

hints: 끝에 e가 붙으면 앞의 모음 소리가 어떻게 달라지는지 떠올려요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: tape처럼 끝에 e가 있으면 a를 /에이/로 읽고 e는 소리 내지 않아요. tap의 a는 짧게 읽어요.

questions.prompt: 다음 중 끝의 e를 소리 내어 읽는 낱말이 아니라 읽지 않는 낱말은?
hints: 끝에 e가 있지만 소리 나는 e와 소리 나지 않는 e를 구분해요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: rope의 끝 e는 읽지 않고 o만 /오우/로 길게 읽어요. he, we, me는 e를 /이/로 읽어요.

questions.prompt: Which word does not belong in the -ig family?
hints: 끝의 두 글자 ig를 확인해 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: big, dig, wig는 모두 -ig로 끝나요. dog는 -og로 끝나서 가족이 아니에요.

questions.prompt: Which word does not belong with hop, top and mop?
hints: 세 낱말과 끝부분 글자가 같은지 비교해요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: hop, top, mop은 -op로 끝나요. pop, stop, shop도 -op로 끝나지만 map은 -ap로 끝나서 다른 가족이에요.

questions.prompt: Which word belongs to the -ug family with bug, hug and rug?
hints: 끝 두 글자 ug가 같아야 해요. 첫 글자는 달라도 돼요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: jug(주전자)는 -ug로 끝나서 bug, hug, rug와 한 가족이에요.

questions.prompt: Which word does not belong: make, bake, mask, rake?
hints: 끝 세 글자를 소리 내어 비교해 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: make, bake, rake는 -ake로 끝나요. mask는 -ask로 끝나요.

questions.prompt: Which word does not belong: hill, will, mall, mill?
hints: a가 들어간 낱말이 하나 있어요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: hill, will, mill은 -ill로 끝나요. mall은 -all로 끝나요.

questions.prompt: 박수를 한 번만 치면 되는(마디가 한 개뿐인) 동물 이름은?
hints: tiger는 ti-ger처럼 나눠 읽어요. 나눌 수 없는 낱말을 찾아요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: horse는 한 마디로 읽어요. tiger, rabbit, monkey는 두 마디예요.

questions.prompt: 박수를 두 번 치는(마디가 두 개인) 음식 이름은?
hints: 마디마다 입이 열리는 횟수를 세어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: pizza는 piz-za로 두 마디예요. rice는 한 마디, banana와 potato는 세 마디예요.

questions.prompt: Which animal name has a different number of syllables: zebra, frog, duck, bear?
hints: 세 개는 박수 한 번, 하나만 박수 두 번이에요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: zebra는 ze-bra 두 마디이고, 나머지는 한 마디예요.

questions.prompt: 마디가 세 개인 동물 이름은?
hints: 낱말을 천천히 나누어 마디를 세어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: kangaroo는 kan-ga-roo로 세 마디예요. tiger와 panda는 두 마디, horse는 한 마디예요.

questions.prompt: 대문자로 쓴 PIG를 소문자로 바꾸면?
hints: P와 비슷하게 생긴 소문자 q, b와 헷갈리지 않게 조심해요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: PIG의 P, I, G를 소문자로 바꾸면 p, i, g, 곧 pig예요.

questions.prompt: 소문자로 쓴 milk를 모두 대문자로 바꾸면?
hints: 세 번째 글자 L(엘)과 I(아이)의 모양을 구분해요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: m-i-l-k를 차례로 바꾸면 M-I-L-K, 곧 MILK예요. L은 I와 달라요.

questions.prompt: 대문자 낱말과 소문자 낱말이 같은 낱말인 짝은?
hints: 글자를 하나씩 비교해서 달라진 글자가 없는 짝을 찾아요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: BIRD의 글자를 소문자로 바꾸면 bird예요. 나머지는 소문자로 바꿔도 서로 다른 낱말이에요.

questions.prompt: Look at the b_rd in the tree. It can sing. 빈칸에 알맞은 글자는?
hints: 새를 뜻하는 낱말의 철자를 떠올려요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: bird는 b-i-r-d예요. 나무에서 노래하는 새이므로 i가 알맞아요.

questions.prompt: We eat sandwiches at the pic_ic in the park. 빈칸에 알맞은 글자는?
hints: 공원에서 음식을 먹는 나들이를 뜻하는 낱말이에요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 공원에서 샌드위치를 먹는 picnic(소풍)은 p-i-c-n-i-c으로 써요.

questions.prompt: It is cold. I wear a warm ha_ on my head. 빈칸에 알맞은 글자는?
hints: 머리에 쓰는 물건이라는 문맥을 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 머리에 쓰는 따뜻한 것은 hat(모자)이에요. ham은 음식이라 맞지 않아요.

questions.prompt: sun의 첫 글자 s를 f로 바꾸면 어떤 낱말이 될까요?
hints: 첫 글자 하나만 바뀌고 나머지 두 글자는 그대로예요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: s를 f로 바꾸면 f-u-n, 곧 fun(재미)이 돼요. 가운데 u는 그대로예요.

questions.prompt: bed의 마지막 글자 d를 g로 바꾸면 어떤 낱말이 될까요?
hints: 바꾸는 글자는 끝의 하나뿐이에요. 가운데 e는 그대로예요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: d를 g로 바꾸면 b-e-g, 곧 beg(애원하다)예요.

questions.prompt: Change one letter in 'pen' to make an animal that lays eggs.
hints: 첫 글자만 바꿔요. 알을 낳는 동물이 힌트예요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: pen의 p를 h로 바꾸면 hen(암탉)이에요. 암탉은 알을 낳아요.

questions.prompt: 여러 개를 말할 때 낱말 끝에 -es를 붙이는 낱말은?
hints: 끝 글자가 x, s, sh, ch인 낱말을 찾아요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: x로 끝나는 낱말은 -es를 붙여 boxes처럼 써요. cat, dog, pen은 -s만 붙여요.

questions.prompt: 복수형 끝의 s가 /s/('스') 소리로 나는 낱말은?
hints: s 앞의 소리가 목을 울리는 소리인지 생각해 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: hats는 /t/ 뒤라서 s를 /스/로 읽어요. dogs, pens, bags는 /즈/로 읽어요.

questions.prompt: We wash two ___ after lunch. 빈칸에 알맞은 낱말은?
hints: two가 나오니 여러 개를 뜻하는 형태가 필요하고, sh로 끝나는 낱말의 규칙을 떠올려요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: dish는 sh로 끝나서 복수형은 -es를 붙인 dishes예요. two가 있어 복수형이 필요해요.

questions.prompt: walk에서 읽지 않는 글자는?
hints: 낱말을 소리 내어 읽을 때 빠지는 소리를 찾아요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: walk는 /워크/처럼 읽어서 l은 소리 나지 않아요.

questions.prompt: 입술을 붙였다 떼며 '프' 하고 내는 /p/ 소리로 시작하는 낱말은?
hints: 입술이 맞닿는 소리 /p/와 /b/는 비슷하지만 달라요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: pear는 /p/로 시작해요. bear는 /b/, dear는 /d/, tear는 /t/로 시작해요.

questions.prompt: 뱀이 내는 'ssss' 소리, 곧 /s/로 시작하는 낱말은?

questions.prompt:
Paper is made from wood, and the process has several steps. First, trees are cut down and taken to a factory. There the wood is broken into small pieces and mixed with water. The mixture is heated until it becomes a soft, thick liquid called pulp. Next, the pulp is spread on a screen and pressed flat, and the water is removed. The reasons why trees must never be cut down
The ways schools collect and sort old paper

The first bicycle was made in the early 1800s. It had no pedals, so riders pushed it along the ground with their feet. Later, pedals were added to the front wheel, but these bikes were very hard to ride. The modern bicycle, with two wheels of the same size and a chain, was developed in the 1880s. They pulled it with a horse.
They pushed it with their feet.

Dear students and families,

Best wishes,
Ms. Ahn

Bats are active at night, when it is too dark to see well. So how do they avoid trees and catch insects? Many bats use sound. As they fly, they make very high squeaks that people usually cannot hear. The sound travels through the air, hits an object, and bounces back as an echo. The bat's ears catch the echo, and its brain uses it to tell how far away the object is and how big it is. This ability is called echolocation. Some bats can even notice an insect as thin as a hair. Scientists have studied this ability for many years.

Why people cannot hear very high squeaks

Why leaves turn different colors in autumn

This pollen is carried to other flowers, helping plants grow fruit and seeds. Many foods we enjoy, such as apples, almonds and strawberries, depend on this work. Sadly, the number of bees is falling in many places because of lost habitat and certain chemicals. Scientists suggest planting more flowers in gardens and avoiding strong chemicals. Even a few pots on a balcony can give hungry bees a place to feed.

She has to attend a morning meeting
The students eat breakfast at school

questions.prompt:

He had left it on the bus.

questions.prompt:
Everyone yawns, yet scientists still cannot fully explain why. For years, people believed yawning brings extra oxygen to a tired body. hints: 문제가 무엇을 묻는지 한 문장으로 말해 본 뒤 보기를 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: year는 시간을 나타내는 선행사라서 관계부사 when을 써요.

questions.prompt:
Complete the sentence.
"Nobody understands the reason ___ the shop closed so early."
hints: 문제가 무엇을 묻는지 한 문장으로 말해 본 뒤 보기를 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: reason을 선행사로 하는 관계부사는 why예요.

questions.prompt: Which sentence has a noun clause used as its subject?

options.text: She studies in a quiet place near the lake.
What she wants is a quiet place to study.
She likes to study when the house is quiet.
The quiet place where she studies is open.

hints: 문제가 무엇을 묻는지 한 문장으로 말해 본 뒤 보기를 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: What she wants is a quiet place to study.에서 What she wants(그녀가 원하는 것)가 주어 역할을 하는 명사절이에요. 나머지 문장에는 주어 역할을 하는 명사절이 없고, 장소를 꾸미는 절이나 때를 나타내는 절이 있어요.

questions.prompt: In "I doubt that he will come," the clause "that he will come" works as...

options.text: an adverb of time in the sentence
the object of the verb doubt

hints: 문제에 나온 “ the clause ”에 집중해서 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: that절은 doubt의 목적어 자리에 온 명사절이에요.

questions.prompt: "This is the lab where they test new batteries." Which phrase can replace "where" without changing the meaning?
hints: 문제에 나온 “where”에 집중해서 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: where = 전치사 + which예요. which만 쓰면 전치사 in이 빠져 틀려요.

questions.prompt: "Where does Mina live?" Which sentence reports this question correctly?

options.text: He asked where does Mina live.

hints: 문제에 나온 “Where does Mina live?”에 집중해서 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 간접의문문은 「의문사 + 주어 + 동사」 순서이고 do/does를 쓰지 않아요. 주어 Mina에 맞춰 lives를 써요.

questions.prompt:
Complete the sentence.
"The coach hasn't decided ___ the new player will start the match."
hints: 문제가 무엇을 묻는지 한 문장으로 말해 본 뒤 보기를 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: ‘~인지 아닌지’를 뜻하는 명사절은 whether로 이끌어요. 나머지는 뒤의 절이 완전해서 알맞지 않아요.

questions.prompt: In which sentence is "that" a conjunction that starts a noun clause?

options.text: I knew that she would call.
That book is on the table.
The song that she sang was lovely.

hints: 문제에 나온 “that”에 집중해서 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: I knew that she would call에서 that은 knew의 목적어절을 이끌어요. 나머지는 지시어이거나 관계대명사예요.

questions.prompt:
Complete the sentence.
"I'm afraid ___ we have run out of tickets."
hints: 문제가 무엇을 묻는지 한 문장으로 말해 본 뒤 보기를 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: afraid 뒤에서 말하는 내용을 이끄는 접속사는 that이에요.

questions.prompt:
Which part has an error?
"Do you know / what time / does the film start / tonight?"
hints: 문제가 무엇을 묻는지 한 문장으로 말해 본 뒤 보기를 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 간접의문문이므로 what time the film starts의 평서문 어순이어야 해요.

questions.prompt:
Combine the two sentences:
"I don't know." + "Where did he put the key?"

options.text: I don't know where he put it the key.
I don't know where he put the key.
I don't know that he put the key.
I don't know where did he put the key.

hints: 문제에 나온 “I don't know.”에 집중해서 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 두 문장을 합칠 때 의문문은 평서문 어순의 where절이 되고, did는 사라지며 동사가 과거형으로 바뀌어요.

questions.prompt:
Combine the two sentences:
"She is pleased." + "Her team won the final."

options.text: She is pleased that her team winning the final.
She is pleased her team that won the final.
She is pleased what her team won the final.
She is pleased that her team won the final.

hints: 문제에 나온 “She is pleased.”에 집중해서 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 감정 형용사 pleased 뒤에 이유를 나타내는 that절이 와요.

questions.prompt:
다음 문장에서 whether가 이끄는 절의 역할은?
"I can't decide whether I should join the club."

options.text: 문장 전체의 주어 역할을 하는 절

hints: 문제가 무엇을 묻는지 한 문장으로 말해 본 뒤 보기를 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: decide는 ‘무엇을’ 결정하는지를 목적어로 취하고, whether절이 그 목적어 역할을 해요.

questions.prompt:
Complete the sentence.
"Tell me the reason ___ you changed your mind."
hints: 문제가 무엇을 묻는지 한 문장으로 말해 본 뒤 보기를 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: reason 뒤의 관계부사는 why예요.

questions.prompt:
Complete the sentence.
"We were surprised ___ the old bridge was still open."
hints: 문제가 무엇을 묻는지 한 문장으로 말해 본 뒤 보기를 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: surprised 뒤에는 놀란 이유를 말하는 that절이 와요.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is a correct indirect question for "What time is it?"

options.text: Could you tell me that time it is?
Could you tell me what time it is?
Could you tell me what is time it?
Could you tell me what time is it?

hints: 문제에 나온 “What time is it?”에 집중해서 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 간접의문문은 「의문사구 + 주어 + 동사」 순서예요.

questions.prompt: "The fact ___ she apologized surprised everyone." Choose the correct word.
hints: 문제가 무엇을 묻는지 한 문장으로 말해 본 뒤 보기를 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: fact의 내용을 설명하는 동격 that절이에요.

questions.prompt: 다음 중 “I'll never forget how kind she was.”의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?

options.text: 나는 그녀가 친절하게 지내던 방법을 잊지 못할 거예요.
나는 그녀가 얼마나 친절했는지 결코 잊지 못할 거예요.
나는 그녀처럼 친절했던 적이 한 번도 없어요.

hints: 문제가 무엇을 묻는지 한 문장으로 말해 본 뒤 보기를 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: how kind she was는 ‘그녀가 얼마나 친절했는지’라는 뜻의 명사절이에요.

questions.prompt: In which sentence does "what" mean "the thing that"?

options.text: What a lovely view this is!
I like what you wrote in the card.
What time does the train leave?

hints: 문제에 나온 “what”에 집중해서 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: I like what you wrote in the card.의 what you wrote는 ‘네가 쓴 것’이라는 뜻의 관계대명사 what절이에요. 나머지는 의문문이나 감탄문이에요.

questions.prompt: In "The news that he had won made his parents proud," the word "that"...

options.text: introduces a clause that states what the news is
replaces the noun news inside its own clause
means the same as the word this
works as the object of the verb had won

hints: 문제에 나온 “ the word ”에 집중해서 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 이 that은 news의 내용을 설명하는 동격절을 이끄는 접속사이고, 절 안에서 별도의 문장 성분이 아니에요.

questions.prompt:
Complete the sentence.
"Their decision depends on ___ the weather improves."
hints: 문제가 무엇을 묻는지 한 문장으로 말해 본 뒤 보기를 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 전치사 on 뒤에는 whether절을 쓸 수 있고, that절은 올 수 없어요.

questions.prompt:
Complete the sentence.
"Please tell me ___ the best way to learn English vocabulary is."
hints: 문제가 무엇을 묻는지 한 문장으로 말해 본 뒤 보기를 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: is 뒤가 비어 있으므로 보어 자리를 채우는 what이 알맞아요.

questions.prompt: Which sentence about planting a tree contains a grammar error?

options.text: I remember the place where we planted this tree.
I remember when we planted this tree.
I remember that we planted this tree.
I remember the day where we planted this tree.

hints: 문제가 무엇을 묻는지 한 문장으로 말해 본 뒤 보기를 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: day는 시간을 나타내므로 where가 아니라 when이어야 해요.

questions.prompt: Which sentence about a late train contains an error?

options.text: He asked me why the train was late.
He wondered why was the train so late.
I know that the train was late.
He wondered why the train was so late.

hints: 문제가 무엇을 묻는지 한 문장으로 말해 본 뒤 보기를 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 간접의문문은 why the train was ~의 평서문 어순이어야 해요.

questions.prompt: "I agree with what she said at the meeting." What does "what she said" mean?
hints: 문제에 나온 “ What does ”에 집중해서 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: what은 ‘~하는 것’이라는 뜻이라 what she said는 ‘그녀가 말한 것’이에요.

questions.prompt: "The teacher didn't say when the test would be held." Which sentence is closest in meaning?

options.text: The teacher did not explain why we need the test.
The teacher did not give the date of the test.
The teacher said the test was already over.
The teacher told us the test would never be held.

hints: 문제가 무엇을 묻는지 한 문장으로 말해 본 뒤 보기를 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: when the test would be held는 ‘시험이 언제 열릴지’이므로 날짜를 말하지 않았다는 뜻이에요.

questions.prompt:
Complete the sentence.
"Midnight is the moment ___ the new year begins."
hints: 문제가 무엇을 묻는지 한 문장으로 말해 본 뒤 보기를 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: moment는 시간 선행사이므로 관계부사 when이 알맞아요.

questions.prompt: “나는 그녀가 왜 화가 났는지 모르겠다.”를 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?

options.text: I don't know what she is angry.
I don't know why is she angry.
I don't know why she is angry.
I don't know she why is angry.

hints: 문제에 나온 “나는 그녀가 왜 화가 났는지 모르겠다.”에 집중해서 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: why가 이끄는 간접의문문은 「why + 주어 + 동사」 순서예요.

questions.prompt: “그곳은 우리가 처음 만난 카페이다.”를 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?

options.text: That is the café where we first met.
That is the café when we first met.
That is the café where we first met there.
That is the café which we first met.

hints: 문제에 나온 “그곳은 우리가 처음 만난 카페이다.”에 집중해서 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: 장소 선행사 café 뒤에 완전한 절이 오면 where를 써요. where가 ‘거기서’의 뜻을 포함해요.

questions.prompt:
Which word can follow "possibility" in this sentence?
"The possibility ___ the plan may fail worries me."
hints: 문제에 나온 “possibility”에 집중해서 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: possibility의 내용을 설명하는 동격 that절이에요.

questions.prompt:
Complete the sentence.
"It is a pity ___ you can't join us."
hints: 문제가 무엇을 묻는지 한 문장으로 말해 본 뒤 보기를 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: It is a pity that ~는 ‘~라니 안타깝다’라는 뜻의 가주어 구문이에요.

questions.prompt:
Complete the sentence.
"She asked me ___ I needed a ride."
hints: 문제가 무엇을 묻는지 한 문장으로 말해 본 뒤 보기를 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: ‘~인지 아닌지’를 묻는 목적어절은 if나 whether로 이끌어요.

questions.prompt: "Are you hungry?" he asked. Which sentence reports this correctly?

options.text: He asked me whether was I hungry.
He asked me that I was hungry.
He asked me if was I hungry.
He asked me whether I was hungry.

hints: 문제에 나온 “Are you hungry?”에 집중해서 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: yes/no 질문은 whether(if)로 전달하고, 평서문 어순을 써요.

questions.prompt: In "He showed me the house where he was born and told me that he missed it," which is a noun clause?

options.text: the house where he was born

hints: 문제가 무엇을 묻는지 한 문장으로 말해 본 뒤 보기를 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: that he missed it은 told의 목적어절이에요. where he was born은 house를 꾸미는 절이에요.

questions.prompt: In which sentence does "how" start a noun clause?

options.text: How did she bake the cake?
I learned how she baked the cake.

hints: 문제에 나온 “how”에 집중해서 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: I learned how she baked the cake.의 how she baked the cake는 learned의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절이에요.

questions.prompt:
Complete the sentence.
"That is ___ many students choose to study abroad."
hints: 문제가 무엇을 묻는지 한 문장으로 말해 본 뒤 보기를 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: That is why ~는 ‘그것이 ~하는 이유예요’라는 뜻이에요.

questions.prompt: What does "Whatever you decide is fine with me" mean?

options.text: Any choice that you make is fine.
I will go wherever you go.
I wonder if you will decide.
The reason you decide is not clear.

hints: 문제가 무엇을 묻는지 한 문장으로 말해 본 뒤 보기를 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 읽고 알맞지 않은 것부터 지워 보세요.
questions.explanation: whatever you decide는 ‘네가 무엇을 결정하든’이라는 뜻의 명사절이에요.

questions.prompt: 다음 중 that이 접속사로 쓰인 문장은?

options.text: The movie that we saw was long.
She said that she was tired.

questions.prompt:
Hanji is a traditional Korean paper made from the inner bark of the mulberry tree. Making it by hand takes many steps. First, the bark is boiled and beaten until it turns into soft fibers. Mixed with water and a natural plant glue, these fibers are scooped onto a screen and shaken gently, forming a thin, even sheet. Dried in the sun, the sheets become strong yet light. Because of this strength, hanji has been used for doors, windows, books, and even clothing. questions.prompt:
Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, yet they support about a quarter of all sea life. Built slowly by tiny animals called corals, a reef can take thousands of years to form. The corals live together with algae, which give them food and bright colors. When the water becomes too warm, stressed corals push out the algae and turn white, a process called bleaching. Bleached reefs are not dead, but they are weak. Given enough time and cooler water, they can recover. Unfortunately, warming seas, polluted rivers, and careless tourists, touching or breaking the coral, make recovery difficult in many places. Protecting reefs therefore requires action at local and global levels.

What is the passage mainly about?

options.text: Why algae are more important than corals

How rivers carry sea animals to the open ocean
Why coral reefs matter and what puts them at risk

questions.prompt:
Walking across a stone bridge built five hundred years ago, you may wonder why it is still standing. The answer lies in its shape. Unlike a flat beam, an arch pushes the weight outward and downward, spreading the load along curved stones. Pressed tightly together, the stones lock in place, and the heavier the load, the tighter they hold. Builders of the past, working without modern math, learned these lessons by trial and error. Failed bridges taught them what worked. Today, engineers still copy the arch, though they build it with steel and concrete. Having proved its strength for centuries, the arch remains one of the safest shapes in construction.

What is the main point of the passage?

options.text: Flat beams are the safest shape for long bridges.
The arch shape explains why old bridges stay strong.
Past builders used math to make perfect bridges.
Modern engineers have stopped using stone for bridges.

However, experiments showed that breathing more oxygen does not stop yawns. A different theory suggests that yawning cools the brain. This could explain why people yawn more often when they are tired or bored, since the brain may run slightly warmer at those times. Yawning is also contagious: seeing someone yawn often makes us yawn too. Researchers think this may be linked to empathy. In other words, our bodies may react to the people around us without our noticing.

One explanation is that a printed page has a fixed shape, so readers remember where an idea appeared, such as near the top of the left-hand page. On a scrolling screen, the words move and this mental map is harder to build. Another reason is that screens invite quick skimming. This does not mean that digital reading is useless; it simply means that for a difficult text we should ______.

Which phrase best fills the blank?

options.text: avoid reading long texts on paper or screen altogether
read only on screens with bright lights
choose a format that supports careful reading
always skim every text quickly to save time at school

questions.prompt:
Hana had saved for weeks to buy a bicycle, but when she reached the shop, the price had risen. She walked home slowly, trying not to cry. At the door, her neighbor, Mr. Park, was waiting with an old blue bicycle. “My legs are too stiff for riding now,” he said, “and it seems a waste to leave it in the garage.” Hana looked at the scratched frame and the worn seat, and then she smiled. It was not the shiny bicycle she had imagined, but it was better, because someone had thought of her. That evening she rode around the whole neighborhood until the street lights came on.

How did Hana feel at the end of the story?

questions.prompt:
To the Editor:

I am writing about the recent decision to shorten the opening hours of our public library. According to the notice, the change will save the city a small amount of money. However, many students depend on the library as a quiet place to study after school, and several older residents use its computers to read the news and keep in touch with relatives. Closing at five o'clock instead of eight will make the library useless to most of these people. I urge the city council to reconsider and to look for savings in other areas.

Sincerely,
Minho Seo

options.text: To announce a new library opening
To ask the council to change its decision
To advertise computers for older residents
To thank the city for saving money

questions.prompt:
When we hear the word courage, we usually imagine a firefighter running into a burning building. That kind of bravery is dramatic and easy to admire. There is, however, a quieter form of courage that appears in everyday life: telling the truth when it is uncomfortable, admitting a mistake, or asking for help. These actions rarely win applause, and nobody writes songs about them. Yet they require us to face fear in the same way, because we risk looking weak or being rejected. Perhaps we should learn to value this ordinary courage as much as the heroic kind.

Songs should be written about daily life.
Firefighters are braver than most other kinds of workers.
Everyday courage deserves as much respect as heroism.

questions.prompt:
When a tree is cut down, its trunk shows a pattern of circles called rings. Each ring usually represents one year of growth. In a year with plenty of rain, the tree grows quickly and forms a wide ring. In a dry year, growth slows, and the ring is thin. When a honeybee finds a rich patch of flowers, it must tell the rest of the hive where to go. It does so with a remarkable dance. Back inside the hive, the bee moves in a figure-eight pattern and shakes its body along the middle line. The angle of this "waggle" shows the direction of the flowers compared with the sun, while its length conveys the distance. A longer waggle means the food is farther away. Other bees crowd around the dancer, touching it with their antennae to pick up the message. They then fly out to forage in the right place. Scientists once doubted that insects could communicate in such detail, but careful experiments have confirmed it. The system is especially useful when food is scarce nearby, because a single scout can guide hundreds of workers to a distant meadow within a few hours.

questions.prompt:
Traditional Korean houses were heated by ondol, a system that warms the floor instead of the air. Many people take photos of everything they see, believing that the pictures will help them remember. Psychologists, however, have found the opposite. In one experiment, visitors to a museum were asked to photograph some objects and only look at others. Later, they remembered fewer details about the objects they had photographed. questions.prompt:
Climbers who go above three thousand meters often feel dizzy, tired or short of breath. For this reason, experienced mountaineers climb in stages, spending a few nights at middle heights before going higher. Those who rush upward risk altitude sickness, which can be serious. questions.prompt:
When one ant finds food, it does not call the others. Instead, it walks back to the nest leaving a faint trail of chemicals. Other ants smell the trail and follow it, and each one that finds food adds more chemicals on the way home. questions.prompt:
Every winter, city workers spread salt on roads and sidewalks. The reason is simple: salt lowers the temperature at which water freezes, so ice melts even when the air is below zero. As a result, accidents drop and buses keep running. However, this solution has a hidden cost. When the snow melts, the salty water flows into the soil and nearby streams. Young trees along busy roads often turn brown in spring because their roots cannot take in enough water from salty ground. Salt also speeds up rust on cars and bridges, which means higher repair bills. Some towns therefore mix the salt with sand or sprinkle it only on the most dangerous hills and corners. Safety clearly matters most, but careful use lets towns protect people without damaging the places they live in.

They become soft in cold drinks.
They last for hundreds of years in the sea.

questions.prompt:
Many people joke that weather forecasts are always wrong, but the truth is more interesting. A forecast of rain tomorrow is right most of the time, because computers can track large systems of clouds and wind across the whole planet. The further into the future we look, however, the less reliable the prediction becomes. Small errors in today's measurements grow bigger each day, so a seven-day forecast is much less certain than a one-day forecast. This is why forecasters often say 'a 30 percent chance of rain' instead of 'it will rain'. The number does not mean that it will rain on thirty percent of the city; it means that, on days with similar conditions, rain fell about three times out of ten. People who ignore this advice may feel cheated when a sunny day follows a warning. In fact, the forecast may have been correct. A fair judgment requires many days, not one.

Why is a seven-day forecast less certain than a one-day forecast?

options.text: Forecasters stop working after the first day of the week.
Small measurement errors grow larger as time passes.
Wind systems disappear after twenty-four hours have passed.
Computers cannot track clouds for more than a single day.

hints: 질문의 핵심 낱말: “forecast”. 지문에서 같은 낱말이나 비슷한 뜻의 말을 찾아보세요.
지문의 중간 부분에 단서가 있어요. 그 부분을 다시 읽어 보세요.
questions.explanation: 'Small errors in today's measurements grow bigger each day'라고 나와요.

questions.prompt:
Every year, dictionary editors announce a list of new words, and every year some readers protest. They believe a dictionary should protect the language, not follow its changes. The editors disagree. A dictionary, they say, is like a map: it does not decide where the roads go, it records where people actually walk. A word is added only after careful observation. Editors collect examples from books, news articles and speech, and they wait to see whether the word appears for several years in many different places. A funny expression used by a few friends for one summer will not qualify. For example, 'selfie' entered dictionaries only after it had become common in several countries. Some words also leave the book when nobody uses them, although this happens slowly. Critics may still complain, but the process is a record of the community's habits rather than a judgment about good or bad English.

Only when readers vote for it each summer.

The building's residents' committee, however, listened to every worry, invited an experienced beekeeper to answer questions, and agreed to a six-month trial. The bees flew toward the city's parks, not toward the balconies, and the only visible change was a row of flowerpots that tenants planted to feed them. questions.prompt:
A tide pool looks calm, yet life there is anything but easy. Twice a day, the sea retreats and leaves small basins of water on the rocks. Animals living in these pools must survive hot sunshine, sudden rain, and waves that crash against them without warning. Sea stars hold on with hundreds of tiny tube feet, limpets clamp themselves tightly to the stone, and crabs hide in cracks until the water returns. Even the water itself changes quickly: as it warms under the sun, it loses oxygen and grows saltier, a combination that would kill many ocean animals within hours. The creatures of the tide pool have adapted to this, which makes them valuable to scientists. By studying how they cope with sudden change, researchers hope to predict how other sea life might respond as oceans grow warmer.

options.text: Which sea animals are most dangerous to people visiting the shore
How tide-pool animals survive rapid changes in their surroundings
How scientists build artificial pools in laboratories for research
Why the sea leaves small basins on the rocks twice every day

questions.prompt:
Working from home has changed how people think about the office. Employees save hours of commuting, spend more time with family, and can often arrange their day to match their energy. Employers, meanwhile, save on rent and can hire people from distant cities. Yet the arrangement has costs that are easy to overlook. New workers miss the casual conversations through which experienced colleagues pass on unwritten rules. Creative teams find that brainstorming through a screen is slower and less spontaneous. Scientists use the word "microplastics" for plastic fragments smaller than five millimeters. Some are made that small on purpose, such as the beads once added to certain face scrubs. Others form slowly as larger items, including bottles, bags, and fishing nets, break down in sunlight and waves. Washing synthetic clothing also releases tiny fibers that pass through household drains. Because the pieces are so small, they are hard to remove from water, and they can be swallowed by animals at every level of the food chain, from plankton to fish. Researchers are still investigating whether the particles harm human health, and results so far are mixed. Even so, many countries have limited the sale of products containing plastic beads, and some manufacturers now sell washing machine filters that trap fibers. These steps will not solve the problem alone, but they show that practical solutions exist.

questions.prompt:
Most people have sent a message that autocorrect has turned into nonsense, but the feature does far more good than harm. Behind the scenes, the software compares what you type with a large list of words, estimates which word you probably meant, and replaces the error before you press send. Modern versions also learn from your habits: they remember the names of your friends, the slang you use, and the phrases you often repeat. The system is not perfect, because it cannot read your mind and it sometimes mistakes a rare word for a mistake. Experts therefore advise users to read quickly before sending any important message. They add that the tool should support careful writing, not replace it. Ironically, people who rely on it completely may notice their own spelling skills slowly weaken.

Autocorrect should be removed from every phone and computer

When my family moved to the city, I missed the open fields behind our old house. The concrete, the traffic, and the crowds felt endless. Then my grandmother discovered a community garden at the end of our street. Each family there rents a small plot, and everybody shares the tools, the compost, and the knowledge. At first I only carried water cans, but soon Mr. Alvarez, the oldest gardener, taught me how to sow carrots, tie tomato plants to stakes, and tell weeds from seedlings. Supporters say that a common outfit reduces pressure to follow expensive fashion, helps students feel part of one community, and saves families time each morning. Critics reply that uniforms limit self-expression and can be uncomfortable, especially in hot weather. A recent survey of one thousand students found that fifty-four percent preferred wearing uniforms, while forty-six percent opposed them. Interestingly, the opinions varied more by school than by age. Teachers in the study reported that discipline did not noticeably change, but several noted that fewer arguments about clothing took place. Researchers conclude that the effect of uniforms is real but modest, and that local conditions probably matter more than any general rule.

Which word best describes the tone of the passage?

questions.prompt:
The watch had not worked for years, but Grandfather never stopped winding it. Every evening, after supper, he took it out of the drawer, turned the tiny crown a few times, and held it to his ear as if listening for a heartbeat. When I asked why, he only smiled. After he passed away last spring, my mother gave it to me. Yesterday, curious, I took it to a repair shop. The watchmaker opened the case and found a folded scrap of paper tucked inside, written in Grandfather's careful handwriting: "Time is only worth keeping when someone is waiting to share it." I carried the watch home in my palm, and for the first time since the funeral, I cried and smiled together.

Which word best describes the mood of the ending?

At nine o'clock sharp, forty employees gathered in the conference room to discuss the company's most urgent problem: too many meetings. A cheerful manager opened with a slide titled "Reducing Meetings Through Meetings." Everyone nodded gravely. Over the next two hours, we agreed that a committee should be formed to study the issue, that the committee would meet weekly, and that a follow-up meeting would be scheduled to review the committee's progress. Lena: Oh, hello. Is there a problem?
Mr. Okoro: Not a problem exactly. It is just that, around eleven, I hear something rolling across the floor. Like marbles.
Lena: Marbles? Ah. That would be my cat. She has a ball with a bell inside, and she goes wild at night.
Mr. Okoro: I see. I did suspect an animal. It is only that I start work at five, and I have had trouble sleeping this week.
Lena: I am so sorry, I had no idea it carried. I can put the ball away before ten, and I will put a rug in the hallway.
Mr. Okoro: That would be very kind. Truly, I do not want to cause trouble. I like having a neighbor who waters the plants on the stairs.

Unfailingly upbeat, whatever the caller says

questions.prompt:
Ari: Hi, Bo. Great to see you at last. We have been meeting since Monday.
Bo: I know, I know. Things came up. What did I miss?
Ari: Not much. Only the outline, the survey, and most of the slides, which we finished last night.
Bo: Oh wow, that is fast. Thanks, you guys are amazing.
Ari: Yes, we are. Anyway, your section was supposed to be the conclusion. Did you start?
Bo: Almost. I have the title.
Ari: The title. Excellent. I am sure the audience will be moved by the title.
Bo: Okay, that was unkind.
Ari: Was it? I have been awake since six doing the charts. I would rather be unkind than do your part, too.
Bo: Fair. I will write it tonight and send it by nine.
Ari: Nine, then. If it does not arrive, I will present the conclusion myself and leave your name off the slide.
Bo: Understood. Nine, no later.

What is Ari's tone when talking about the title?
hints: 이 글을 한 문장으로 줄이면 무엇에 관한 글일까요? 처음과 마지막 부분을 함께 살펴보세요.

questions.explanation: 'the audience will be moved by the title'는 제목뿐인 Bo의 진척을 비꼬는 말이에요.

questions.prompt:
Dr. Hale: Good morning, Mateo. How are we feeling today?
Mateo: Honestly? Terrible. I read the scan report last night and it had so many long words that I stopped reading.
Dr. Hale: Ah. Reports are written for other doctors, not for people reading them at midnight. Let me translate.
Mateo: Please.
Dr. Hale: The scan shows a small crack in the bone of your wrist. It is clean, it has not moved, and it should heal on its own with a cast.
Mateo: A cast? For how long?
Dr. Hale: About six weeks. You will be able to write with your other hand, and I would suggest a good excuse to let someone else carry your bag.
Mateo: Six weeks. I am in a band.
Dr. Hale: Guitar?
Mateo: Drums.
Dr. Hale: Then I am sorry, but I am not worried. Your drumming will be back, and sooner than you think. Your patience, I am afraid, will need exercise.

Which pair of words best describes Dr. Hale's manner?

I wanted to love Midnight Orchard, a card game in which two to four players race to harvest apples before dusk falls. The box is beautiful: the illustrations glow, the cards feel thick and smooth, and the wooden apple tokens are a delight to hold. For the first twenty minutes, my friends and I were enchanted. Then the rules began to fray. A card that lets you "swap any two orchards" turned out to contradict the instruction on the next page, and we spent a quarter of an hour arguing over the booklet instead of playing. Even when we agreed, the game dragged; one round took almost an hour, and by the end the winner seemed less thrilled than relieved. Would I recommend it? Disappointed, though still appreciative of the design
Confused and unable to form an opinion

[1] In fact, researchers have found that the brain uses sleep to store what it has learned during the day. [2] Because of it, students who sleep well after studying usually remember more facts than those who stay awake until morning. [3] The effect is especially strong for difficult material, such as new vocabulary or math formulas. [4] A sensible routine, therefore, is to finish studying at a reasonable hour and protect at least eight hours of rest. Even a short nap after class can give the brain a small chance to organize new information. Parents and teachers can help by encouraging regular bedtimes during exam weeks instead of praising students who study until dawn.

What does "The effect" in the fourth sentence refer to?

options.text: Students remembering more after a good night's sleep
Students scoring higher because they study for longer
Students finding new vocabulary easier to spell aloud
Students feeling tired after studying all night long

questions.prompt:
Does reading stories make people kinder? Some psychologists believe it can. When we read a novel, we follow a character's thoughts, fears and choices for hours, and this practice may help us imagine how others feel. In several studies, people who had just read a short story scored slightly higher on tests that ask them to read emotions in photographs of eyes. Not every researcher is convinced. Good communication is not only about speaking well; it also depends on how well we listen. Researchers on conversation often describe "active listening," which means giving full attention to the speaker instead of preparing your own reply. Active listeners show that they care in small ways: they look at the speaker, nod occasionally, and avoid checking their phones. They may also say "I see" or "That sounds difficult" to show that they follow the speaker's feelings. Surprisingly, people who feel truly heard are more likely to trust the listener and to calm down when they are upset.

questions.prompt:
Many people dislike voicemail, yet a well-planned message can save time for everyone. Begin with your name and the reason you are calling, and speak clearly at a steady speed. If you leave a phone number, say it slowly, and repeat it at the end because listeners often need a second chance to write it down. Give one clear request, such as "Please call me back before noon," instead of a long explanation. It is also polite to say when you will be available, so the other person can plan. Finally, thank them and say goodbye briefly. Avoid spending the whole message apologizing or saying "um" again and again. A good message should last no more than thirty seconds, and if it takes longer, consider sending a text or an email instead.

What is the main idea?

options.text: People should never leave a phone number.
Phone calls are more polite than emails.
Voicemail is always better than a text message.
A short, clear voicemail makes communication easier.

questions.prompt:
In school projects, disagreement is almost unavoidable, but it does not have to lead to an argument. The key is to separate the idea from the person. Instead of saying, "That's a terrible plan," try, "I see what you mean, but I'm worried about the cost." Beginning with a point of agreement shows that you have listened. You can then use a softener such as "I'm not sure that..." or "Maybe we could..." to offer your alternative gently. It also helps to ask questions: "What do you think would happen if we changed the date?" This invites the other person to think with you rather than defend himself. If the discussion becomes heated, it is wise to take a short break. Often the best solution is a mixture of both ideas.

What does the writer mean by "separate the idea from the person"?

options.text: Avoid speaking about plans at all
Work in different rooms from your partner
Criticize the plan, not the one who suggested it
Let one person make every decision

Light conversations with strangers can make people feel better.

If someone says, "You gave a great presentation," answering "No, it was terrible" may make the speaker feel embarrassed, because it seems to reject their opinion. A better response is, "Thanks, I'm glad you enjoyed it." You may add a short comment, such as "I worked on it all weekend," to continue the conversation. Doing business with people from other countries can be rewarding, but small cultural differences can cause misunderstanding. In some countries, arriving ten minutes early to a meeting shows respect. In others, the host may expect guests to arrive a little late, and starting exactly on time can feel rushed. Exchanging business cards is also treated differently. In several Asian countries, people offer and receive a card with both hands and read it carefully before putting it away. Writing on it or pushing it into a back pocket may seem impolite.

Experts advise that the best strategy is not to memorize every rule but to stay curious. Ask polite questions, watch how others behave, and be ready to adjust. Showing a sincere interest in other customs usually matters more than getting every detail right.

It is impossible for young workers to manage
It is less important than showing interest
It should be done before any meeting

questions.prompt:
Welcome to your first week at Harbor Hotel. Guests form their first impression at the front desk, so your behaviour matters a great deal.

Always greet guests with a smile within ten seconds of their arrival, even if you are on the phone. Use their family name when you have it. When a guest has a complaint, listen without interrupting, apologize for the inconvenience, and say clearly what you will do about it. Never promise something you cannot deliver; if you are unsure, say that you will check with your manager and give a time when you will reply.

Remember, too, that guest information is private. Do not say a guest's room number aloud in the lobby. Write it down and hand it over instead.

Guests who stay at the hotel

First, they research the organization. Knowing what a company makes, whom it serves, and what it values allows you to connect your own skills with its needs. Second, they practise answering common questions aloud, such as “Tell me about a time you solved a problem.” A good answer gives a brief situation, describes the action you took, and explains the result. Every parcel that reaches your door has passed through a chain of steps in a distribution center. When a truck arrives, workers first check the delivery note against the number of boxes to make sure nothing is missing. The goods are then unloaded and scanned, which records their arrival in the computer system.

Next, each parcel is sorted by destination. Large centers use conveyor belts and machines for this task, while smaller ones depend on workers who read the labels. Sorted parcels are placed into containers, which are loaded onto vans according to their route. Finally, drivers scan every parcel again when it leaves the building and when it reaches the customer. This final scan allows the sender to follow the delivery online.

Because mistakes at any stage can delay a parcel, workers are trained to check labels carefully and to report damaged boxes immediately.

questions.prompt:
Freelancers are self-employed workers who take on jobs for different clients rather than working for one employer. Writers, designers, translators, and programmers often choose this path because it offers freedom. A freelancer can decide when and where to work, and which projects to accept.

However, this freedom comes with trade-offs. Income can change greatly from month to month, so many freelancers keep savings to cover quiet periods. They are also responsible for tasks that an employer would normally handle, such as sending invoices, paying taxes, and finding new clients. For those who are considering this option, a sensible first step is to start part-time while keeping a regular job, and to build a reputation slowly.

Its author is unnamed, and the page is full of links to buy supplements. Result two comes from a university medical center. Titled "Diet and Mood: What the Research Shows," it was reviewed by two named doctors in March and lists twelve studies at the bottom. It says the evidence is promising but not yet conclusive. Result three is a forum thread where a user writes, "My cousin ate bananas daily and was cured." The student must decide which source to trust for a school presentation.

Why should the student be careful with result one?

options.text: It lists too many studies for readers to follow
Its author is unknown and it seems to be selling something
Its title is too long to fit on one screen
It was reviewed by doctors who disagree with each other

hints: 질문의 핵심 낱말: “student”. 지문에서 같은 낱말이나 비슷한 뜻의 말을 찾아보세요.
보기를 하나씩 지문과 비교하며 맞지 않는 곳에 표시해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 익명 저자와 보충제 판매 링크는 신뢰도를 떨어뜨리는 단서예요.

questions.prompt:
Every evening, millions of teenagers scroll through short videos that last less than fifteen seconds. Critics claim that this habit is damaging our ability to concentrate, and many parents agree. However, the evidence is thinner than the headlines suggest. Most studies show only that heavy users of short videos also tend to struggle with long tasks; they do not show which came first. A student who is already bored by homework may simply reach for the phone more often. What is clear is that apps are designed to keep us watching, using endless scrolling and automatic replay. Rather than blaming the format, we should ask who benefits when we stop choosing what to watch and let a machine decide.

What is the writer's main argument?

options.text: The link to weak attention is unproven, but app design deserves scrutiny
Long videos are always better for learning than short ones
Short videos should be banned for everyone under the age of eighteen without exception
Parents are wrong to worry about how teenagers use phones

hints: 질문이 무엇을 묻는지 먼저 한 문장으로 말해 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 지문과 비교하며 맞지 않는 곳에 표시해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 인과가 입증되지 않았지만 앱 설계는 따져 봐야 한다는 것이 글쓴이의 주장이에요.

questions.prompt:
A dramatic photo of a subway station filled with brown water has been shared more than 80,000 times this week, with captions claiming it shows yesterday's storm in our city. Our team ran the image through a reverse image search and found the same picture in a news archive from 2019. It was taken in another country, after a pipe burst under a main road. Local transit officials confirmed that none of our stations flooded during yesterday's rain. The photo itself is real, but the claim attached to it is false. We contacted several accounts that shared it; two have deleted their posts, and one has added a note explaining the mistake. Rating: Misleading.

Why is the claim rated "Misleading"?

options.text: A real photo was presented as proof of an event it does not show
The photo was created by a computer program
The photo showed a storm that was much worse than the captions claimed
The photo showed a station that does not exist

hints: 질문의 핵심 낱말: “misleading”. 지문에서 같은 낱말이나 비슷한 뜻의 말을 찾아보세요.
보기를 하나씩 지문과 비교하며 맞지 않는 곳에 표시해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 사진은 진짜지만 다른 시기·장소의 것이라 설명이 사실과 달라요.

questions.prompt:
Last month, the finance manager of a small company received a call from what sounded exactly like her chief executive. The voice asked her to transfer 20,000 dollars to a new supplier at once, and to keep the matter confidential. She complied. Only later did she discover that the caller had used software to copy the executive's voice from a public interview. Experts warn that such "voice cloning" scams are spreading because only a few seconds of audio are needed. They advise organizations to agree on a secret code word, to call back on a known number before sending money, and to be suspicious of any request that combines urgency with secrecy. "A familiar voice is no longer proof of identity," said one researcher.

What is the main point of the article?

Company executives should avoid giving public interviews or speeches
Finance managers are usually careless with money
Phone calls are always safer than written messages
